title: Basic credentials in an Authorization header
summary: A synthetic Basic user-pass, Base64-encoded as one token, after the Basic scheme in an Authorization request header, in a raw request, with a lowercase scheme and doubled space, and inside a quoted command-line header argument.
rationale: The password is inside an encoded token, so its exact source span is the whole token: a span over only part of it, or only the decoded password, does not exist in the source. The header name and scheme are the carrier and stay outside the span; in the quoted form the closing quote is not part of the token.

expectation.rationale: Flag, with the token after the scheme as the extent. RFC 7617 defines the credentials as the Base64 of user-id, a single colon and password, so the token is the carrier of the password; the header syntax is the token68 grammar of RFC 9110.

sources.supports: the client constructs the user-pass by concatenating the user-id, a single colon (":") character, and the password, and obtains the basic-credentials by encoding this octet sequence using Base64

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
